stories.headline: US cancels G20 group photo as allies refuse to stand with Russia
body: Marco Rubio scrapped the traditional 'family photo' at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta.
About a third of countries, including the UK and Australia, said they would boycott or walk out rather than pose with Russia's Sergei Lavrov.
Rubio still opened the talks with a call for unity on global security and trade.
stories.joke: Nobody wanted to be in the photo. The group chat is going to be awkward.
stories.vc: Open splits at the G20 make global trade deals harder, which keeps markets wary of new tariffs.

image.credit: Embassy of the United States of America to Italy / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Iran calls US outreach 'a positive step' as talks move to Qatar
body: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said a US push to open dialogue is a positive step, but no meetings with US officials are planned yet.
Iran studied JD Vance's letter and set out its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
An Iranian delegation went to Doha, a day after Qatari mediators visited Tehran.
stories.joke: Progress in diplomacy: everyone's now talking about talking.
stories.vc: Hormuz reopening would ease oil prices fast, the single biggest swing factor for India's import bill.

stories.statLabel: years of dispute over the court
stories.headline: Riot police at Poland's top court after its chief judge is suspended
body: Riot police faced protesters outside Poland's constitutional court after its contested president and his deputy were suspended.
Government-appointed judges made the move in a decade-long fight over whether the court is legitimate.
President Karol Nawrocki was seen struggling to enter the building; the opposition PiS party reacted furiously.
stories.joke: When the court needs a court to decide if it's a court.
stories.vc: Rule-of-law fights affect EU funding for Poland, one of Europe's fastest-growing economies.

image.credit: Lukas Plewnia from Berlin, Deutschland / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Walmart probes Flipkart staff over ₹150 crore in alleged kickbacks
body: Walmart is investigating whistleblower claims that Flipkart employees took over ₹150 crore from vendors.
Vendors allegedly got better visibility on the platform in return, in the smartphones and luggage categories.
It is Walmart's third such probe at Flipkart in under three years; Flipkart says it is committed to governance.
stories.joke: Paid placement, just not the kind the finance team signed off on.
stories.vc: Governance issues before a likely Flipkart IPO could weigh on its valuation with public investors.

stories.headline: Electric two-wheeler sales rise again; TVS and Hero gain
body: India registered 2.15 lakh electric two-wheelers in October, up 2.9% from September and 48% from a year ago.
TVS leads with a 27.2% share; Hero MotoCorp grew fastest, reaching 13.4% and closing in on Ather.
Bajaj, Ather and Ola saw monthly declines, with Ola down 13.7%.
stories.joke: The scooter wars: old giants are quietly lapping the startups.
stories.vc: Legacy makers winning EV share puts pressure on startups like Ola and Ather to show profits, not just growth.

stories.headline: Bengaluru plans a full makeover of Silk Board junction
body: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda told officials to draw up a permanent plan for the Central Silk Board junction.
It should improve traffic flow, pedestrian paths and public spaces.
He also launched 'Ward One', a campaign to fix junctions and local infrastructure across 43 wards.
stories.joke: Silk Board: Bengaluru's most famous traffic jam may finally get a glow-up.
stories.vc: Better junctions around the Outer Ring Road help the tech parks that sit along it.

stories.headline: OpenAI reportedly cuts its new funding target to $20 billion
body: OpenAI has lowered the target for its new round to $20 billion, from a reported $30 billion, the FT says.
The WSJ says it has secured $11 billion so far, led by investors from the UAE.
It had been reported raising at valuations of $1.25–1.4 trillion ahead of a planned IPO.
stories.joke: Even trillion-dollar companies have to settle for a smaller cheque sometimes.
stories.vc: A softer raise for the leading AI lab hints investors are getting pickier about AI valuations.

image.credit: European Commission - Photographer: Aurore Martignoni / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Unhedged: why Wall Street's dealmaking boom is fading
body: The FT's Unhedged podcast says the year's merger boom has started to slow.
There were megadeals like the $111 billion Paramount–Warner Bros Discovery tie-up.
But higher borrowing costs and softer markets have cooled the appetite for new deals.
stories.joke: Bankers' bonuses are watching this trend very closely.
stories.vc: Fewer M&A deals mean fewer exits for VCs and private equity, which slows new fundraising.

stories.headline: TikTok is quietly turning into a super app
body: TikTok has added restaurant guides and is reportedly building in-app payments over direct messages.
It already has TikTok Shop, local maps, games and better search.
The goal looks like a 'super app', like China's WeChat.
stories.joke: First it took your evenings. Now it wants your wallet and your dinner plans.
stories.vc: Super apps keep users and payments in one place, a model India's Paytm and PhonePe also chase.

stories.headline: Apple's new CEO: we won't ship AI for AI's sake
body: Apple CEO John Ternus told Wired he likes where Apple stands in AI, despite criticism that it's behind.
Apple will 'absolutely' use AI in products, he said, but only where it truly helps users.
Ternus took over as CEO at the start of September.
stories.joke: Translation: we'll ship AI when it's ready, and it'll be called something else.
stories.vc: Investors want proof Apple's slower AI approach won't cost it iPhone upgrades.

stories.headline: Judge lets NAACP lawsuit over xAI's data centre pollution go ahead
body: A federal judge refused to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit against xAI over its Colossus data centre near Memphis.
The suit says xAI ran at least 35 gas turbines without required air permits.
xAI argued the turbines were mobile and exempt.
stories.joke: Turns out 'they have wheels' isn't a permit.
stories.vc: Power and permits are now the real bottlenecks for AI data centres, and a growing legal risk for investors.

stories.headline: Yemen's new fighting puts thousands of pregnant women at risk
body: At least 290,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting flared again in August, the UN says.
Among them are 6,100 pregnant women, 600 of them due to give birth within two weeks.
The UN has sent mobile teams and midwives to camps as food and fuel prices soar.
stories.vc: Maternal care is among the first services to collapse in conflict; aid funding for it is chronically short.

stories.headline: Why divorce is financially harder on women
body: Journalist Melinda Wenner Moyer told NPR that divorce often leaves women much worse off financially.
Her reporting for New York Magazine was titled 'The Strong, Empowered, Secretly Broke Divorcee'.
She argues 'equal' divorce laws can still be unfair in a society where women earn less.
stories.joke: Freedom feels great. Splitting the bills, less so.
stories.vc: Women's lower earnings and career gaps for care work compound over a lifetime; planning tools for women are an underserved market.

stories.headline: An Ohio ad about a candidate's childhood abuse angers women voters
body: A Vivek Ramaswamy ad features Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother saying Acton lied about documented childhood abuse.
Ohio women told The 19th they felt revulsion, but not surprise.
They question whether using sexual abuse against women in politics is ever disqualifying.
stories.vc: How voters react to such tactics shapes whether more women run for office at all.

stories.headline: Max Healthcare to add 209 beds with ₹415 crore
body: Max Healthcare approved ₹415 crore to add 209 beds across three hospitals in the Delhi region.
That's 85 beds at Max Noida, 60 at Vaishali and 64 at BLK-Max, plus a multi-level car park at BLK-Max.
It follows a quarter with 20% revenue growth.
stories.joke: More beds, and finally somewhere to park.
stories.vc: Adding beds to existing hospitals is the cheapest, fastest way for chains to grow, and investors reward it.

stories.headline: Indira IVF in talks to buy Kerala's Sabine Hospital
body: Indira IVF, India's largest IVF hospital chain, is in talks to buy Sabine Hospital, a Kerala chain for fertility and mother-and-child care.
The deal could value Sabine at ₹1,200–1,300 crore; Indira IVF may take a 70–75% stake.
Owner CX Partners bought about 54% in 2024 at a valuation of about ₹835 crore.
stories.joke: Fertility clinics: the one healthcare business literally built on growth.
stories.vc: Private equity is consolidating specialty hospital chains, with fertility care among the hottest segments.

stories.headline: Paras Healthcare lists at a 4% premium
body: Shares of hospital chain Paras Healthcare listed at ₹720, about 4% above the ₹693 issue price.
They rose as much as 7.9% during the day, valuing the company at about ₹8,007 crore.
The IPO raised ₹500 crore in fresh money and was subscribed 2.23 times.
stories.joke: A steady debut. Exactly what you want from a hospital.
stories.vc: Hospital IPOs give chains cash to build new beds; a calm debut keeps the listing window open for others.

stories.headline: AIIMS Nagpur gets ₹30 crore for a high-security virus lab
body: AIIMS Nagpur got ₹30 crore from the National Centre for Disease Control to build a Biosafety Level-3 lab.
It will help detect and study high-risk infectious diseases in the region.
It should be ready in about a year and cut reliance on NIV Pune.
stories.joke: Not a new wing for patients, but one for the germs, under strict lock.
stories.vc: Regional testing labs shorten outbreak response times, which lowers the cost of epidemics.
